questions.q: A participant joins a recreational basketball program, enjoys learning new skills and develops new friendships. Which mental-fitness benefits are most clearly demonstrated?
options: Achievement and social connection.
Increased physiological arousal only.
Reduced access to activity.
Elimination of all future stress.
questions.feedback: Skill development can provide achievement, while shared activity can strengthen social connection.

sources.organisation: Australian Sports Commission Clearinghouse for Sport
sources.title: Social and Mental Wellbeing

questions.q: A coach records athlete fatigue, enjoyment and progress each week. When fatigue rises and performance falls, the coach reduces training load and increases recovery. What does this best demonstrate?
options: Using the same program regardless of feedback because consistency is more important than individual athlete responses.
Monitoring athlete responses and making individual program adjustments
Replacing coaching judgement with athlete preference
Reducing standards whenever training becomes difficult
questions.feedback: Good program design includes monitoring athlete responses and adapting training and recovery when needed.

sources.title: Training load and recovery position statement

questions.kk: Benefits of Regular Participation in Movement
questions.q: Which outcome is a physical benefit of regular participation in physical activity?
options: Improved muscular strength and endurance
A stronger sense of purpose in life
Greater ability to recognise and manage emotions
More opportunities to develop supportive friendships
questions.feedback: Improved muscular strength and endurance are physical benefits because they improve the functioning and capacity of the body.

sources.title: Sport, physical activity and our health

questions.q: A qualified female referee reports repeated sexist remarks from spectators at community matches. The association says the number of women registered as referees has increased, so its gender-equity strategy must be successful. What is the most appropriate evaluation and response?
options: Use referee registrations as the sole measure of success because more women joining means they must feel welcome.
Recommend that the referee ignore the comments and continue officiating; complaints might discourage spectators.
Assess retention and reports of harassment, enforce spectator-conduct procedures and provide accessible reporting and support.
Reduce the number of matches assigned to women until spectators become accustomed to seeing female officials.
questions.feedback: More registrations do not establish that referees experience respectful, equitable conditions. Monitoring retention, safety and complaint outcomes alongside participation data helps assess inclusion; clear behaviour standards, reporting and support address the identified harassment rather than placing the burden on officials.

increasing physical training volume immediately before competition to improve sporting performance.

avoiding thoughts about an upcoming performance.
questions.feedback: Imagery involves mentally rehearsing movements, sensations or situations and can support confidence and concentration.

questions.q: What does a gender pay gap in sport refer to?
options: A difference in training volume between teams
A difference in athlete age
A difference in competition rules between sports
A difference in sporting earnings between genders
questions.feedback: A gender pay gap is a difference in earnings between genders. Sporting income may include salaries, prize money and sponsorship.

questions.q: Which example best distinguishes muscular strength from muscular endurance?
options: Both involve only joint range of motion and therefore depend mainly on the flexibility available around the working joints
Strength focuses on peak force, whereas endurance focuses on sustaining repeated or prolonged muscular work.
Strength uses oxygen while endurance never does.
Endurance is required only in cardiovascular exercise.
questions.feedback: Muscular strength concerns maximum force production, while muscular endurance concerns sustaining muscular work over time.

questions.q: Student reflection: 'I was nervous about joining the gym, but my friends started coming with me and kept encouraging me to attend.' Which factor is most directly enabling participation?
options: Community
Peers
Gender
Family support
questions.feedback: The friends are peers whose encouragement and shared attendance increase motivation and commitment.

questions.q: A workplace wants to reduce prolonged sitting. Which initiative best reflects the Social-Ecological Model?
options: Send one detailed email explaining that prolonged sitting is harmful and expect employees to independently change their daily behaviour
Ask employees to rely on motivation alone.
Install standing desks but make no other changes.
Combine education, team movement breaks, accessible standing options and a procedure supporting regular breaks.
questions.feedback: The strongest option addresses individual knowledge, social support, physical environment and policy together.

questions.kk: Prevalence and Trends of Physical Activity, Physical Inactivity and Sedentary Behaviour
questions.q: A worker sits for eight hours, completes a 45-minute run after work and then watches television for three hours. Which statement best describes the day?
options: The person is not sedentary because they completed a run.
The person can accumulate physical activity while also spending substantial time sedentary.
The run means all health risks associated with prolonged sitting are removed.
The person must be physically inactive because they sat at work.
questions.feedback: Physical activity and sedentary behaviour are independent enough that both can occur within the same day.
